name: nav-menu
description:
The full-screen menu a narrow `navbar` opens: a marine glass layer over the whole page with the nav points centred and set very large.

A SEPARATE composite, and the reason is structural rather than tidiness. The bar is `backdrop-filter` glass, and a filtered element creates a containing block for `position: fixed` descendants — so a menu nested inside the bar is trapped inside the bar's box and covers nothing. The real header found this and renders the menu as a SIBLING of the header, with the bar kept above it so its close control still closes it. Any implementation that nests this inside `navbar` will look correct in a test harness and fail on the actual page.

The type is the design. `clamp(2.25rem, 11vw, 3.75rem)` in the display face is not a heading treatment borrowed for a menu — at this size a menu of five items IS the page, which is what makes a full-screen menu worth having over a dropdown.

base.$description:
`position: fixed` over the whole viewport at the overlay layer — BELOW the bar, deliberately, so the bar's close control stays reachable and the menu cannot cover the thing that dismisses it.

It IS a container, like every other composite. `inset: 0` gives it a width from outside its contents, which is the one precondition containment needs, so there is no reason for this unit to be the exception — and one good reason against: the type below sizes in `cqi`, so the menu renders correctly at any size it is given rather than only at full screen. A `vw`-based menu is right exactly once and wrong in a preview, a split pane, or a tablet sidebar.

scrim.$description: Marine at 90% with a heavy blur behind it. Not opaque: the page staying faintly visible is what says the menu is ON the page rather than a different one, so dismissing it feels like closing rather than navigating back.

item.$description: The display face at `clamp(2.25rem, 11cqi, 3.75rem)`. `cqi` — the container's inline size — not `vw`. The real header uses `11vw` and is right by coincidence: there the menu happens to BE the viewport. Measured against its own container it is right everywhere, including the place `vw` visibly failed — this unit's own specimen, rendering at 3.75rem inside a 324px card.

footer.$description: What sits under the nav points — the language switch on the real header. Smaller, because it is a setting and not a destination.

tone.$description: The ground the menu lays over.

solid.$description: No blur — for a surface where the page behind is noise rather than context, and for the browsers that cannot do it.

selected.$description: The page you are already on, in the accent ink — the one colour on a marine ground that is neither the foreground nor a dimmed version of it.

reducedMotion.$description: The menu still opens and the items are still there — only the rise and the stagger go. Removing the transition entirely would be fine; removing the ANIMATION without this would leave every item at `opacity: 0`, which is the classic reduced-motion bug: the movement is the only thing that was revealing the content.

a11y.note:
A dialog in everything but name: while it is open, focus is trapped inside it, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the toggle that opened it. The page behind it is `inert` — without that, a screen reader and a Tab key both walk straight through the scrim into a page the sighted user cannot see.

ONE navigation landmark, not two. The menu holds the same links the bar does, so it must be the same `<nav>` moved rather than a hidden second copy; two landmarks with the same label is a screen reader announcing the navigation twice and a keyboard user tabbing through it twice.

`visibility: hidden` rather than `display: none` in the closed state, so the open transition has something to animate from — and so the closed menu is genuinely removed from the tab order, which `opacity: 0` alone does not do.
